title: Dejar de + infinitive: leaving the countryside

sections.content: You know *dejar de* + infinitive from B1 Unit 12: it means to stop doing something you did before (*dejé de fumar*). With *no*, *no dejar de* + infinitive means to keep on doing it (*no dejo de cocinar en casa*). Both are useful for migration: what people stopped doing when they left the countryside, and what they kept doing.

items.spanish: Millones de personas dejaron de vivir en el campo.
items.english: Millions of people stopped living in the countryside.

items.spanish: Muchos campesinos dejaron de trabajar la tierra y buscaron empleo en una fábrica.
items.english: Many peasants stopped working the land and looked for a job in a factory.

items.spanish: Muchos migrantes no dejaron de enviar dinero a su familia.
items.english: Many migrants kept sending money to their family.

items.spanish: Las ciudades no dejaron de crecer.

sections.content: *Dejar de* is always followed by an infinitive, never by a gerund or a noun: *dejaron de vivir*, not *dejaron de viviendo*. Use the preterite (*dejaron de*) for a change that happened at some point, and the imperfect for a habit that stopped slowly.
